Grep of src/ for truncate_messages: the only call is via getattr in _rollback_conversation (tools/query_database.py:237-249), called solely from the `except asyncio.CancelledError` handler (query_database.py:448-456); the other hits are comments/docstrings. The method is synchronous (conversation_store.py:93-124) with no awaits. Counterexample input considered: a second call site or an async store; none exists in src/. The anyio semantics (level-cancellation re-delivered at each await inside a cancelled scope) match the docstring's stated behavior under anyio-driven cancellation; a bare asyncio cancel would not re-deliver, but the docstring's claim is scoped to anyio, and a synchronous method is safe in both cases.

query_database.py:175-192: get-or-create and users += 1 happen with no await between them, before lock.acquire(), so waiters are counted. _release_queue_entry (141-151) deletes only when users<=0 and the registry entry is this one. Hostile input traced: holder plus a parked waiter; the holder releases, users goes 2->1, entry survives, so a new call reuses the same lock rather than minting a second one. Had only holders been counted, the entry would be deleted at that point, as the docstring says. Cancelled waiter: the except BaseException at 183-186 decrements and re-raises; asyncio.Lock.acquire leaves the lock unheld on cancel, so no leak and no double-hold. Holder exit is in finally (190-192). The None conversation_id path is unqueued by design, because the agent mints a private id, so it is outside the same-conversation claim.

query_database.py:175-192. Entry creation and users+=1 (175-179) have no await before the try at 181, so the entry is always covered. Acquire failure or cancellation (183-186) calls _release_queue_entry, which deletes the entry at users<=0 (149-151). Normal exit and body exceptions run the finally (190-192), which releases the lock and the entry. Falsifier: cancellation between acquire() returning and entering the try. Line 188 follows 182 with no await, and asyncio delivers cancellation only at suspension points, so there is no window. In the generator-not-resumed case, __aenter__ runs to the yield with no suspension after it, and an unentered context manager creates no entry. The users count includes waiters, so the entry is not deleted while a waiter is parked. The identity re-check at line 150 stops a stale release from deleting a successor entry. Every entry is therefore deleted once no call holds or awaits it.

Grep shows _CONVERSATION_QUEUES touched only at query_database.py:150-151 (_release_queue_entry), 175 and 178 (_conversation_turn). Hostile case tried: a waiter cancelled in acquire. Its release runs synchronously and cannot be interleaved, and the identity check at 150 guards successor entries. Both functions run on the loop (an async context manager and a sync helper called from it), so the comment holds.
